title: MODBUS over Serial Line Specification and Implementation Guide
notes: RTU framing, timing, termination, biasing. Where the answer to most RS485 will not talk problems actually lives. Grep this PDF for biasing and you get zero hits, then conclude it does not cover biasing. It does. Version agnostic URL, same caveat as the application protocol row. title: Guide to Operational Technology (OT) Security
notes: The OT security reference that is not behind a paywall, unlike IEC 62443. US government work, so this one can actually be mirrored here.

title: The control of hazardous energy (lockout/tagout)
notes: The regulation itself, not a vendor's summary of it. Free, quotable, and the actual legal text behind every LOTO procedure.

title: RP2040 Datasheet
notes: Rare case of a chip datasheet under an open license. Verify the license notice inside the PDF before trusting this row's redistributable=yes.

title: BCM2711 ARM Peripherals
notes: The SoC behind the Pi 4. Register level detail that the Pi documentation site summarizes and loses.

title: ESP32-S3 Technical Reference Manual
notes: Revision moves without the URL changing, which is exactly the case verified_level exists to catch.

title: MQTT Version 5.0
notes: The base spec under Sparkplug. Read the OASIS IPR terms before flipping redistributable.

title: Sparkplug Specification
notes: What makes MQTT usable for plant data: birth and death certificates, state management, the topic namespace.

title: The CIP Networks Library (EtherNet/IP)
notes: Landing page only. The spec itself is sold and it is expensive. Cite it by number, paraphrase structure, never reproduce. A GATED, UNREAD row is still a useful row: it tells a reader the document exists, what it covers, and what it costs.

title: NFPA Free Access to codes and standards
notes: How to legally read NFPA 70, 70E, and 79 for free. A pointer to a viewer, not a document. Never mirror anything reached through it.

title: CLICK PLUS PLC Hardware User Manual
notes: Full manual for the CLICK PLUS PLC line, the low cost brick PLC a lot of small panels and OEM machines use. The landing page itself lists Current version is 1st Ed., Rev. V, Jun 2026, so a tech can confirm freshness before trusting wiring or spec pages. Chapters are individually linked PDFs off this page, for example ch1.pdf, which was confirmed reachable.

title: Productivity1000 User Manual and Inserts
notes: Hardware manual for the Productivity1000 PAC line, covers install, wiring, and the P1000 CPU. A tech opens this for terminal wiring diagrams and module specs when the panel builder did not leave a printed copy. The page states its own current revision and date, which is worth checking against the printed manual in the panel.

title: DL06 User Manual
notes: The DirectLOGIC DL06 is still common on legacy skids and small water and wastewater panels, so this manual is the fastest way to pull relay numbering, addressing, and I/O specs on a system nobody has touched in a decade. Page reports its own revision as 3rd Edition, Rev. I, Oct 2024.

title: SNAP PAC S-Series Controller User's Guide
notes: Install and use guide for the SNAP PAC S1 and S2 rack mount controllers still running in a lot of water, oil and gas, and building automation sites. Covers install, LED status codes, and firmware update steps, the things a tech actually needs standing in front of the rack.

title: PAC Control User's Guide
notes: The programming manual for PAC Control, the free flowchart based IDE Opto 22 ships for its PAC and groov controllers. A tech pulls this open to look up a specific command's syntax rather than hunting through the software help.

title: groov RIO Universal I/O User's Guide
notes: Covers the groov RIO edge I/O modules, Opto 22's newer DIN rail remote I/O with a built in web server for configuration, no separate software install needed. Useful when a tech is standing at a remote skid with just a laptop and a browser.

title: ControlLogix 5580 and GuardLogix 5580 Controllers User Manual
notes: The core reference for the ControlLogix 5580 family that runs most modern data center and large industrial control racks. A tech opens this for chassis power budgeting, module keying rules, and controller status indicator meanings during a fault call.

title: CompactLogix 5380 and Compact GuardLogix 5380 Controllers User Manual
notes: Covers the CompactLogix 5380 platform, the compact DIN rail Logix controller commonly found on smaller machine and process skids. Same value as the ControlLogix manual but for the smaller footprint hardware, module wiring and status code lookups on site.

title: Micro800 Programmable Controllers General Instructions Reference Manual
notes: The full instruction set reference for Micro800 controllers, ladder, structured text and function block, the entry level Rockwell family found in small OEM panels. A tech uses this to look up a rung's exact instruction behavior instead of guessing from the software autocomplete.

title: PowerFlex 520-Series Adjustable Frequency AC Drive User Manual
notes: Covers the PowerFlex 520 series which includes the very common PowerFlex 525, likely the single most encountered VFD on a plant floor. A tech pulls this for parameter numbers, fault codes, and wiring terminal layout during a drive trip call.

title: Modicon M221 Logic Controller Programming Guide
notes: Programming guide for the Modicon M221, Schneider's small book style logic controller programmed with EcoStruxure Machine Expert Basic. A tech opens this for the instruction list and function block reference when writing or troubleshooting a small machine program.

title: TwinCAT 3 Basics
notes: Introductory manual to TwinCAT 3, Beckhoff's PC based automation and PLC engineering environment for their EtherCAT I/O and motion hardware. Good starting document for a tech coming from a traditional PLC background who now has to open a TwinCAT project.

title: ACS580 Standard Control Program Firmware Manual
notes: Firmware and parameter manual for the ACS580, a common general purpose ABB drive on pump and fan applications. A tech uses this for the full parameter list and fault code table when the drive keypad alone is not enough to diagnose a trip.

title: MELSEC iQ-F FX5U CPU Module Hardware Manual
notes: Hardware manual for the FX5U, Mitsubishi's mid range micro PLC, covering module specs, wiring, and installation. A tech pulls this for terminal layouts and I/O specs on FX5U based machines, common in packaging and machine builder work.

title: SYSMAC CP Series CP2E CPU Unit Hardware User's Manual
notes: Hardware manual for the Omron CP2E, a compact PLC common on European built OEM machines. A tech uses this for wiring diagrams, expansion unit rules, and mounting specs when the machine builder's documentation is missing or in another language.

title: SYSMAC CP Series CP1E/CP2E CPU Unit Instructions Reference Manual
notes: The instruction set reference shared by the CP1E and CP2E families, the actual ladder instruction behavior a tech needs when reading or editing a program rather than just wiring the rack. Companion document to the W613 hardware manual above.

title: WAGO I/O System 750 PFC200 (750-8202) Manual
notes: Manual for the PFC200 2ETH RS controller, WAGO's Linux based DIN rail PAC widely used in building automation and process skids for its native web configuration and CODESYS runtime. A tech opens this for the fieldbus coupler wiring and system LED status table.

title: 1910 Subpart S - Electrical
notes: The general industry electrical rule set (design safety standards plus safety related work practices, sections 1910.301 through 1910.399). A field tech opens this to find the actual regulatory text behind terms like qualified person and approach boundary, not a summary of it.

title: 1910.269 - Electric power generation, transmission, and distribution.
notes: Governs utility scale power generation, transmission, and distribution work: minimum approach distances, grounding, and PPE for line and substation crews. This is the standard a data center or utility side tech is actually held to, distinct from the general industry electrical rule.

title: 1926 Subpart K - Electrical
notes: The construction industry counterpart to 1910 Subpart S, covering temporary wiring, grounding, and electrical work on active job sites. Anyone doing new build or retrofit electrical work under a construction contract is governed by this part, not the general industry one.

title: 1910.212 - General requirements for all machines.
notes: The baseline machine guarding rule, point of operation guards, barrier requirements, and anchoring. Short and general on purpose, it is the citation OSHA reaches for first on an unguarded machine so it is worth having on hand verbatim.

title: 1910.333 - Selection and use of work practices.
notes: Sets the deenergize first rule and the narrow conditions under which energized work is permitted. This is the section that defines when a job actually requires an arc flash study and PPE rather than a simple lockout.

title: 1910.335 - Safeguards for personnel protection.
notes: Requires PPE, insulated tools, and warning signs whenever energized work under 1910.333 is performed. Pair this with 1910.333, one sets when energized work is allowed and this one sets what protects the worker while it happens.

title: Controlling Electrical Hazards
notes: A plain language booklet explaining electrical hazards and OSHA's electrical standards for workers who are not electrical specialists. Good as a toolbox talk handout rather than a citation source, the regulations themselves are the authority.

title: Control of Hazardous Energy Lockout/Tagout
notes: OSHA's own plain language guide to the LOTO standard, with the six basic steps and example tagout procedures. Useful as the training handout that sits next to the regulatory text at 1910.147.

title: DOE Fundamentals Handbook: Electrical Science, Volume 1 of 4
license: public domain (US government work), Distribution Statement A
notes: Free and complete electrical theory training text from the DOE, 166 pages, and it is genuinely open: the title page carries Distribution Statement A, approved for public release, distribution unlimited. The catalog row points at the PDF on energy.gov rather than the standards.doe.gov landing page, which serves HTML and not the document. Dated June 1992 on its own title page, which is why revision_date is empty: the document gives a month, not a day.

title: Recommended Practice: Improving Industrial Control System Cybersecurity with Defense-in-Depth Strategies
notes: CISA's own defense in depth guidance for control system networks: network segmentation, DMZs, and monitoring for PLC and SCADA environments. Written for the same OT boundary a data center or industrial controls tech sits on, and it is free where most OT security guidance is not.

title: NFPA 70E Standard Development
notes: The standard for electrical safety in the workplace, the source of arc flash boundary, incident energy, and PPE category concepts used across the industry. NFPA offers a free read only online viewer of the full text but the document itself must be purchased to download, print, or redistribute.

title: NFPA 70, National Electrical Code (NEC) Standard Development
notes: The National Electrical Code, the base installation and wiring standard behind essentially every electrical inspection in the US. Same access model as 70E, free read only viewer, purchase required for a usable copy.

title: IEC 61850:2026 SER
notes: The series landing page for IEC 61850, communication networks and systems for power utility automation, the protocol family behind modern substation and switchgear IEDs talking to each other. It covers substation automation communication and is sold per part or as the full series through the IEC webstore.

title: ISO 13849-1:2023, Safety of machinery - Safety-related parts of control systems - Part 1: General principles for design
notes: The controlling standard for functional safety of machine control systems, performance levels, category architecture, and safety PLC design. It is the standard behind most safety relay and safety PLC datasheets and is sold as a landing page purchase through iso.org.

title: IEEE Guide for Performing Arc-Flash Hazard Calculations
notes: The mathematical model behind arc flash incident energy calculations, built from over 1800 arc tests and referenced by NFPA 70E as the accepted calculation method. It is the actual engineering standard behind the arc flash labels a tech reads, and IEEE sells it rather than giving it away.

title: UL 508A
notes: The safety standard for industrial control panels, the one a panel builder or field tech checks a UL label against for wire sizing, short circuit current rating, and enclosure construction. Landing page only, the standard itself is a paid UL publication.

title: ANSI/ISA-95.00.01-2025 (IEC 62264-1 MOD), Enterprise-Control System Integration - Part 1: Models and Terminology
notes: The base model for ISA 95, the standard vocabulary and structure for how plant floor control systems interface with enterprise MES and ERP systems. Anyone integrating a PLC or SCADA layer up into a manufacturing execution system eventually runs into this terminology, sold through the ISA store.

title: ANSI/NETA MTS-2023, Standard for Maintenance Testing Specifications for Electrical Power Equipment and Systems
notes: The industry reference for how often and how to test breakers, transformers, relays, and switchgear, the specification most electrical testing companies bid against. Landing page only through the NETA store, this is not a free document.

title: Masterpact MTZ2 / MTZ3 UL Rated/ANSI Certified 800 to 6000 A Circuit Breakers and Switches User Guide
notes: This is the full setup and operation guide for the Masterpact MTZ2/MTZ3 air circuit breaker line used as the main service breaker in a lot of data center and industrial switchgear. A field tech opens this for the MicroLogic X trip unit menu tree, test point wiring, and the mechanical open/close sequence. Downloaded PDF is 49 megabytes so give it time.

title: Masterpact MTZ1 UL Rated/ANSI Certified 800 to 1600 A Circuit Breakers and Switches User Guide
notes: Companion guide to the MTZ2/3 above but for the smaller 800 to 1600 A frame. Same MicroLogic X control unit family so the two documents overlap heavily, keep both because frame size changes physical dimensions and withdrawal mechanism details a tech needs on site.

title: SACE Tmax XT Tmax low voltage moulded case circuit breakers XT5 Operation and maintenance manual for Ekip Touch Trip Units
notes: Operation and maintenance manual for ABB's XT5 molded case breaker with the Ekip Touch trip unit, the touchscreen protection relay ABB puts on its larger MCCBs. A field tech wants this for the trip curve setup screens and the maintenance test procedure, not just the installation drawing that most catalogs give you.

title: Air Circuit Breakers Configuration Manual SENTRON
notes: Configuration manual for the SENTRON 3WL air circuit breaker line, the withdrawable low voltage power breaker Siemens puts in switchgear line ups up to 6300 A. A field tech uses this for the accessory and communication module selection tables since the breaker ships in dozens of trip unit and accessory combinations that are not obvious from the nameplate. No printed document number found on the cover, only the 2012 edition mark, so treat the date loosely.

title: Liebert GXT5 UPS Installer/User Guide 208 V Input, 208 V Output, L1-L2-G (HV)
notes: Install and operate guide for the Liebert GXT5, the online double conversion UPS Vertiv puts in server rooms and small data center power chains. A field tech wants this for the battery replacement procedure and the front panel alarm code list, both of which are missing from the spec sheet.

title: Symmetra PX 10-40 kW and 20 kW 208 V Operation
notes: Operation manual for the Symmetra PX modular scalable UPS, a common three phase UPS in mid size data centers because power modules and batteries hot swap without a shutdown. A field tech opens this for the LED and display alarm meaning table and the module swap sequence, since doing it out of order can drop the load.

title: ASCO 4000 SERIES ATS Automatic Open-Transition Transfer Switches Operator's Manual
notes: Operator's manual for ASCO's 4000 series automatic transfer switch across the D, J, H, G, and F frame sizes, the workhorse open transition ATS behind a lot of standby generator installs. A field tech uses this for the transfer logic timing settings and the exerciser clock programming steps.

title: Medium Voltage Fuses, Various Types, Different Configurations, Many Ratings, One Solution
notes: Full line catalog for Mersen medium voltage fuses covering transformer, motor, and capacitor protection in the Amp-Trap and 9F60/9F62 families. A field tech uses this to cross reference an E-rated or R-rated fuse by physical dimension and interrupting rating when the original nameplate is gone. This is a catalog, not an installation manual, so it will not have torque specs.

title: PowerCommand Transfer Switches Brochure
notes: This is a sales brochure across the whole Cummins PowerCommand ATS family (X series, B series, RA, RSS) not a service manual, and it will not have wiring diagrams or torque values. Still useful for a field tech trying to identify which model family a switch belongs to from the enclosure and door layout before pulling the specific O and M manual, which Cummins gates behind their Power Suite Library login.

title: T-037: PowerCommand Control Application Manual, ANSI Protective Functions
notes: This is the document a field tech actually wants for PowerCommand gear: it lists every ANSI device number protective function the PowerCommand control can run (27, 32, 40, 46, 47, 50/51, 59, 81 and so on) and how each one is set up. Useful across the generator and transfer switch product lines that share the PowerCommand control platform, not just one ATS model.

title: Operation and Maintenance Manual Type RTS30NA Non-automatic Transfer Switches
notes: O and M manual for Russelectric's 30 cycle rated non automatic bypass isolation transfer switch, common in hospital and data center emergency systems where the switch has to carry full fault current through a full transfer cycle without derating. A field tech wants this for the bypass handle interlock sequence, which is easy to get wrong and is the whole safety point of this switch type. Russelectric is now a Siemens brand so the document lives on Siemens infrastructure.

title: I-Line Circuit Breaker Power Distribution Panelboards Information Manual, Class 2110, Instruction Bulletin
notes: Installation and information manual for Square D I-Line panelboards, the bolt on plug in breaker panelboard system found in most commercial and light industrial gear rooms. A field tech uses this for the breaker plug in torque values and the busbar phase sequence, since installing a breaker on the wrong stab position on I-Line gear is a real and common mistake.

title: PowerLogic ION9000 series User manual
notes: User manual for the ION9000, the high accuracy power quality meter Schneider sells for utility revenue metering and data center power monitoring at the switchgear level. A field tech opens this for the CT and PT wiring diagrams and the Modbus register map when integrating the meter into a building power monitoring system.

title: QO and Homeline Load Centers, Instruction Bulletin
notes: Installation instructions for the QO and Homeline residential and light commercial load centers, the small panelboard everyone has in a house or a strip mall unit. A field tech uses this for the conduit hub and ground bar kit compatibility table, and for the tandem breaker slot restrictions that vary by panel model.

title: I-Line II Indoor Busway, Instruction Bulletin
notes: Handling, storage, and installation instructions for I-Line II busway, the plug in bus duct that runs power from switchgear to panelboards through a mechanical room or riser. A field tech uses this for the hanger spacing table and the joint bolt torque values, both of which affect the busway's short circuit withstand rating if done wrong.

title: Dry-Type Transformers 1000 Volts and Below, Instruction Bulletin, Class 7400
notes: Installation and operation guide for Square D low voltage dry type transformers, the step down transformer feeding most 208/120 or 480/277 panels in a commercial building. A field tech opens this for the tap changer setting table and clearance requirements, since dry type transformers need airflow clearance that is easy to shortcut in a tight electrical room.

title: Dry Type General Purpose Power Transformers, Installation Guide
notes: Installation guide for ABB's 150 to 750 kVA low voltage dry type transformers, the ABB counterpart to the Square D dry type bulletin above, useful for comparing tap and clearance specs across the two vendors on the same job. A field tech uses this for the lifting and rigging weight table before a crane pick.
